chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shathawayh al-Mu'addib (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, who said to us: Abdillah ibn al-Mughira said:

I was a Waqifite and performed Hajj with that belief. When I arrived in Mecca, something stirred in my chest, so I held onto the Multazam and said: 'O God, You know my quest and my desire, so guide me to the best of religions.' Then it occurred to me to visit al-Rida (peace be upon him). I went to Medina and stood at his door, and said to the servant: 'Tell your master that a man from Iraq is at the door.' I heard his call (peace be upon him) as he said: 'Enter, O Abdillah ibn al-Mughira.' I entered, and when he looked at me, he said: 'God has answered your prayer and guided you to His religion.' I said: 'I bear witness that you are the Proof of God and the Trustee of God over His creatures.'

key_terms.أَمِينُ اللَّهِ: The Trustee of God, a title for the Imam
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida, referring to Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَمِ: The Multazam, the section of the Kaaba wall between the door and the foundation stone
key_terms.حُجَّةُ اللَّهِ: The Proof of God, a title for the Imam
key_terms.وَقِفِيًّا: A follower of the Waqifiyya sect who believed Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida had died

ai.seo_question: How did Abdullah ibn al-Mughira find guidance to the true religion through Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the transition of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from the Waqifiyya sect to affirming Imam al-Rida’s divine authority, illustrating the concept of *Hujjah* (Proof of God) in Shia theology. The Imam’s immediate recognition of the visitor underscores the infallible knowledge (*‘Ilm*) attributed to the Imams, serving as a key indicator of their leadership (*Imamah*). This event reinforces the Shia belief that true guidance is found through the designated successors of the Prophet.
